historical_references.reference: The Dravids, also known as the Dravidians, are a major ethnolinguistic group native to the Indian subcontinent. The term Dravids is derived from the Sanskrit word Dravida, which originally referred to the three southernmost states of India, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka. According to ancient Indian texts, the Dravidians were the earliest inhabitants of the Indian subcontinent and are believed to have arrived around 5000 BCE.

The Chalukyas were an influential dynasty in Indian history, ruling the Deccan region from the 6th to the 12th centuries CE. They originated from the small village of Vatapi, which is now known as Badami, in present-day Karnataka. The earliest known Chalukya king was Pulakesin I (r. 632-642 CE), and he is said to have belonged to the Dravida race, as mentioned in the Allahabad Inscription.
